subject: Order Form: commercial onboarding — billing & tax routing plan
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire.huang@midlandsys.com>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@midlandsys.com
Date: 2027-10-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Draft order form and questions on billing/tax routing

Hi Sofia —

Thanks for the call this morning. Please find attached our suggested Order Form (v3) — Marco and I flagged a couple of items we need clarified before we route to finance for PO issuance: 

- Invoicing entity: the order form references "Redwood Inference Ltd" but we'll be issuing payment from Midland Systems B.V. — can you confirm which legal entity will appear on invoices and whether currency will be GBP or EUR?
- Taxes: we operate in the Netherlands; we need to confirm whether VAT will be charged by Redwood or reverse-charged to Midland. We attached our VAT certificate (see attachment).
- Payment terms: our procurement policy prefers Net45 for new vendors. The order form shows Net30; is Net45 acceptable for a first-year trial?
- Minimum commit phasing: we'd like a split (60/40) across Q4 and Q1 to help cashflow — is that compatible with your invoicing cadence?

Can you review and advise who on your side needs to sign off (legal vs finance)? We'll need the final PDF to route to our AP team.

Thanks,
Claire Huang
Head of Procurement, Midland Systems
claire.huang@midlandsys.com

Attachment stubs: Midland_OrderForm_Draft_v3.pdf, UK_Tax_Cert_2027.pdf

From: sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@midlandsys.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-10-20T12:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft order form and questions on billing/tax routing

Hi Claire —

Appreciate the clear notes and the VAT cert. Quick answers up front, then internal asks below: 

1) Invoicing entity & currency: We can issue invoices from Redwood Inference EU B.V. (our EU billing entity) with EUR invoices. If Midland requires GBP, we can provide a GBP invoice but it will be processed via our EU entity and may show an FX conversion line.

2) VAT treatment: Based on the VAT cert you attached, we can apply reverse charge (no VAT on Redwood invoice) provided the billing entity and VAT IDs appear on the invoice as required by Dutch law. Kimberly, can you confirm the exact invoice template field we need to populate for reverse charge?

3) Payment terms: Ben — can we make an exception and accept Net45 for this initial trial year for Midland Systems? If yes, we'll note on the order form. If not, what are the implications for revenue recognition and collections?

4) Minimum commit phasing: We can support a 60/40 commit split across Q4/Q1. For invoicing cadence, we typically do monthly invoicing against consumption with a quarterly advance for committed tiers. For your suggested split we can issue two advance invoices (one for the 60% tranche, one for 40%) or alternative: one combined invoice with payment milestones — preference from finance?

Internal next steps: Kim (legal/finance) to confirm invoice template fields and whether EU B.V. is fine; Ben (sales/finance) to confirm Net45 and how we reflect the commit phasing on the order form. Claire — we'll aim to get back with edits to the PDF by EOD Friday so you can route to AP next week.

Sofia Ivanova
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
Mobile: +44 7700 900000

Thanks Sofia / Claire —

Ben here. Short answer: we can accept Net45 for the first-year pilot provided we codify it on the order form and set a calendar reminder for renewal terms ahead of the anniversary. A couple of implementation notes: 

- Revenue recognition: Net45 shifts AR timing but doesn't change committed revenue. Finance is comfortable with Net45 on trial deals under EUR 150k. Since Midland's initial commit is under that threshold, this is fine.
- Commit phasing: We'll reflect the 60/40 split as two staged advance invoices tied to milestone dates (30 Nov 2027 and 15 Jan 2028). That aligns with our collections calendar.
- PO/Remittance: We'll need Midland's PO number on the invoice and the remittance instructions block populated with Midland's entity details (suggested field: "Customer billing entity / PO # / VAT ID").

Kimberly — if you can confirm the invoice template fields for reverse charge and provide an editable PDF of the invoice header I'll drop final redlines into the order form.

Ben Carter
Sr. Sales Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Hi all —

Thanks — I reviewed the VAT cert and the draft order form. Confirmations and deliverables below: 

- Invoicing entity: Redwood Inference EU B.V. will be the invoicing party. We'll include the following fields on the invoice header: Redwood Inference EU B.V. (registered NL entity), our VAT ID NL123456789B01, Customer billing entity, Customer VAT ID, Customer PO number, Invoice currency. 
- VAT handling: Reverse charge is appropriate given Midland's VAT cert. We'll include the standard reverse charge note: "VAT liability to be accounted for by the recipient under Article 194 (reverse charge)." Please ensure Midland's VAT ID is provided on the PO for audit.
- Template: attached is the editable invoice header snippet (InvoiceHeader_snippet.docx) — Ben, please use that when redlining the order form so fields match exactly.
- Net terms approval: Legal and Finance approve Net45 for this first-year pilot. We will add language: "Net45 for Year 1 (trial) — Redwood reserves the right to revert to Net30 thereafter unless mutually agreed in writing."
- Commit phasing & invoicing cadence: We'll record the 60% tranche due as an advance invoice dated 2027-11-30 and the 40% tranche as an advance invoice dated 2028-01-15. Consumption billing will continue monthly thereafter.

Next steps: Sofia to produce a redlined order form (v4) incorporating Net45 and the staged advance invoice dates; Ben to confirm milestone invoice line items; Claire / Midland to provide PO number and final billing entity name (if different from Midland Systems B.V.).

Kimberly Park
